content.text:
The failure is a Jenkins Pipeline bug, not a failed unit/regression test.

`configureAndCompileCRegressions()` defaults `runOptions` to an empty string for the normal candidate C-regression compile. Jenkins does not export `CI_REGRESSION_RUN_OPTIONS` in that case, but the shell runs with `set -u` and expands it unguarded:

```bash
"$CI_REGRESSION_DRIVER" runregression run -c $CI_REGRESSION_RUN_OPTIONS compile
```

Hence:

```text
CI_REGRESSION_RUN_OPTIONS: unbound variable
```

This occurs in “Compile candidate C regressions,” after dependencies, build, unit tests, and candidate installation succeeded. No C regression or later Slurm regression job was submitted.

Fix [Jenkinsfile.stellar_cpu](/Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile.stellar_cpu:380) to tolerate an absent/empty option:

```bash
"$CI_REGRESSION_DRIVER" runregression run -c ${CI_REGRESSION_RUN_OPTIONS:-} compile
```

The `bind` warnings are harmless login-shell noise.

I’ll make the empty option expansion safe in the Stellar Pipeline, then inspect the diff and run the focused CI-script checks available in the repository.

content.text:
Found it. This is another `runregression` path bug, not a numerical failure.

Compilation saves each executable under its execution mode, e.g.:

```text
.../creg-runs/cpu_serial/<test>/<test>
```

But `validate_precompiled_c_regressions()` looks for:

```text
.../creg-runs/<test>/<test>
```

It omits `runMode`. Consequently it reports every precompiled executable as missing and exits before executing any regression. The same defect will also affect the later parallel suite (`cpu_parallel`).

The fix is in [runregression.lua](/Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/gkeyll/lua/Tool/runregression.lua:1180): insert `runMode .. "/"` between `creg-runs/` and the test name.
